Definition: from G303 and G1209; to entertain (as a guest):--receive.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to receive, to take someone in as a guest: Publius, the chief man of Malta, received Paul and his company and lodged them three days courteously — and Hebrews says Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac, he that had received the promises. The same word covers a host opening his house and a father holding on to what God promised.
TheologicalSignificance: Two verses about receiving carry no doctrine of their own; their weight is the welcome — Publius lodging strangers for three days, and Abraham receiving promises he could not yet see.
